- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and then decline too sharply, missing sustained upward momentum.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., 73+ levels) are common, leading to overcorrection downward.
- Model underestimates the final 5–10 days of the 30-day horizon, particularly when true prices show strong upward trend.
- Mean reversion bias: model assumes prices will return to prior levels too quickly, ignoring persistent upward momentum.
- Lagged response: model reacts too slowly to recent price increases, underestimating momentum.
- Forecasts often fail to capture the “late-stage breakout” phase — prices rise faster than model suggests in the final 10 days.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent history” — it overweights recent high prices, leading to inflated forecasts.
